newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products soften with crude.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products soften with crude.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were all weaker on Monday, pressured lower by crude.
Gasoline was softer with futures but found support late in the day after workers called one-day strikes for Tuesday at three French refineries and a go-slow at a fourth.
Unions said they had given notice of strikes on Tuesday at the 200,000 bpd BP refinery at Lavera, the 127,000 bpd La Mede refinery run by Total and Shell's 128,000 bpd Berre refinery.
Arbitrage to the U.S. and tight Italian supplies after Elf scooped up Med material last week also continued to underpin prices.

Naphtha prices were easier with crude with little end user demand to offer support. Traders said interest was still being seen for high paraffinic oil to go transatlantic but some saw rising freight costs starting to restrict this.
Gas oil fell $8.50 a tonne with futures but trade was quiet, traders saying the volatile screen prices discouraging activity.
Attention focussed on an arbitrage to Asia, assessed at around $38 fob Med to Singapore including freight, and an Indian Oil Corp tender for diesel due to be announced later this week.
Heating oil premiums were seen at cif quotes -$0.50 basis Genoa, trending softer on persistent length
"You don't offer. You ask for a bid at very low numbers," one trader said.
High sulphur cracked fuel was pegged steady to a touch softer with activity curtailed because of falling crude futures. Dealers said there was no incentive to trade unless under pressure
"No-one seems sure where crude will settle, so we all wait," said one trader. High sulphur cargoes were pegged comfortably below $110 fob while low sulphur was stable in the low $140s cif Med.
